claim: Humans and other vertebrates define body axis left-right asymmetry in the early stages of embryo development.
source: Humans and other vertebrates define body axis left-right asymmetry in the early stages of embryo development.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about vertebrate development.

claim: The mechanism behind left-right establishment is not fully understood.
source: The mechanism behind left-right establishment is not fully understood.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the current state of scientific understanding.

claim: Symmetry breaking occurs in a dedicated organ called the left-right organizer (LRO).
source: Symmetry breaking occurs in a dedicated organ called the left-right organizer (LRO) and involves motile cilia generating fluid-flow therein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about where symmetry breaking occurs in vertebrate development.

claim: Symmetry breaking involves motile cilia generating fluid-flow in the LRO.
source: Symmetry breaking occurs in a dedicated organ called the left-right organizer (LRO) and involves motile cilia generating fluid-flow therein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of symmetry breaking.

claim: It has been a matter of debate whether the process of symmetry breaking relies on a chemosensory or a mechanosensory mechanism.
source: However, it has been a matter of debate whether the process of symmetry breaking relies on a chemosensory or a mechanosensory mechanism (Shinohara et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shinohara et al., 2012.

claim: Novel tailored manipulations for LRO fluid extraction in living zebrafish embryos allowed pinpointing a physiological developmental period for breaking left-right symmetry during development.
source: Novel tailored manipulations for LRO fluid extraction in living zebrafish embryos allowed us to pinpoint a physiological developmental period for breaking left-right symmetry during development.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The shortest critical time-window for left-right symmetry breaking was narrowed to one hour.
source: The shortest critical time-window was narrowed to one hour and characterized by a mild counterclockwise flow.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The critical time-window for left-right symmetry breaking is characterized by a mild counterclockwise flow.
source: The shortest critical time-window was narrowed to one hour and characterized by a mild counterclockwise flow.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Emptying the LRO of its fluid abrogates simultaneously flow force and chemical determinants.
source: The experimental challenge consisted in emptying the LRO of its fluid, abrogating simultaneously flow force and chemical determinants.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and its intended effects.

claim: The embryo has an unprecedented recovery capacity to re-fill and re-circulate new LRO fluid after fluid extraction.
source: Our findings revealed an unprecedented recovery capacity of the embryo to re-fil and re-circulate new LRO fluid.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental observations.

claim: Embryos that later developed laterality problems had lower anterior angular velocity and less anterior-posterior heterogeneity.
source: The embryos that later developed laterality problems were found to be those that had lower anterior angular velocity and thus less anterior-posterior heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Replacing the extracted LRO fluid with a physiological buffer resulted in some transitory flow homogenization but no laterality defects unless viscosity was altered.
source: Next, aiming to test the presence of any secreted determinant, we replaced the extracted LRO fluid by a physiological buffer. Despite some transitory flow homogenization, laterality defects were absent unless viscosity was altered, demonstrating that symmetry breaking does not depend on the nature of the fluid content but is rather sensitive to fluid mechanics.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Symmetry breaking does not depend on the nature of the fluid content but is rather sensitive to fluid mechanics.
source: Despite some transitory flow homogenization, laterality defects were absent unless viscosity was altered, demonstrating that symmetry breaking does not depend on the nature of the fluid content but is rather sensitive to fluid mechanics.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The zebrafish LRO is more sensitive to fluid dynamics for symmetry breaking.
source: Altogether, we conclude that the zebrafish LRO is more sensitive to fluid dynamics for symmetry breaking.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: In mouse, frogs, and fish, left-right axis establishment involves fluid movement in a specialized organ called the left right organizer (LRO).
source: In mouse, frogs, and fish it involves fluid movement in a specialized organ called the left right organizer (LRO).
evidence: This is established knowledge about vertebrate development.

claim: In the mouse embryo, cilia driven fluid flow inside the LRO has been proposed to activate either a mechanosensory mechanism in the epithelial cells or to transport morphogens towards the left side of the LRO.
source: In the mouse embryo, cilia driven fluid flow inside the LRO has been proposed to activate either a mechanosensory mechanism in the epithelial cells that constitute the LRO, or to transport morphogens (as dissolved molecules or carried inside extracellular vesicles) towards the left side of the LRO (Nonaka et al., 1998; McGrath et al., 2003; Tanaka et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nonaka et al., 1998; McGrath et al., 2003; Tanaka et al., 2005.

claim: The mechanism of symmetry breaking culminates in asymmetric left-sided calcium signalling at the node cells.
source: While the mechanism is unknown, it culminates in asymmetric left-sided calcium signalling at the node cells and a subsequent conserved Nodal pathway on the left side of the embryo (Tanaka et al., 2005; Takao et al., 2013; Mizuno et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 2005; Takao et al., 2013; Mizuno et al., 2020.

claim: The mechanism of symmetry breaking leads to a subsequent conserved Nodal pathway on the left side of the embryo.
source: While the mechanism is unknown, it culminates in asymmetric left-sided calcium signalling at the node cells and a subsequent conserved Nodal pathway on the left side of the embryo (Tanaka et al., 2005; Takao et al., 2013; Mizuno et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 2005; Takao et al., 2013; Mizuno et al., 2020.

claim: The endpoint of the left-right developmental process is the asymmetric localization of internal visceral organs, such as the heart and liver.
source: The endpoint of this developmental process is the asymmetric localization of internal visceral organs, such as the heart and liver.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the outcome of left-right development.

claim: The transparent zebrafish embryo is a particularly suitable model system enabling flow visualization and subsequent scoring of organ asymmetry in the same individual.
source: The transparent zebrafish embryo is a particularly suitable model system enabling flow visualization and subsequent scoring of organ asymmetry in the same individual.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the zebrafish model system.

claim: Wildtype zebrafish embryos have a stereotyped flow pattern in the LRO (Kupffer's vesicle or KV), exhibiting higher dorsal anterior speed.
source: We and others have shown that wildtype (WT) zebrafish embryos have a stereotyped flow pattern in the LRO (known as Kupffer's vesicle or KV), exhibiting higher dorsal anterior speed (Essner et al., 2005; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005; Supatto et al., 2008; Sampaio et al., 2014; Smith et al., 2014; Ferreira et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Essner et al., 2005; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005; Supatto et al., 2008; Sampaio et al., 2014; Smith et al., 2014; Ferreira et al., 2017.

claim: Deviations from the stereotyped flow pattern due to less cilia or shorter motile cilia predictably generate larvae with wrong laterality outcomes.
source: Our group has demonstrated that deviations from this flow pattern due to less cilia or shorter motile cilia, predictably generate larvae with wrong laterality outcomes, indicating a biological relevance to flow (Sampaio et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sampaio et al., 2014.

claim: The zebrafish LRO has a limited lifetime, from ~2 ss to 14 ss.
source: Although the LRO is an organ with a limited lifetime, from ~2 ss to 14 ss (Oteíza et al., 2008), seminal work unveiled that the zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle is dispensable for left-right establishment after 10 somite stages (ss) (Essner et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Oteíza et al., 2008.

claim: The zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle is dispensable for left-right establishment after 10 somite stages.
source: Although the LRO is an organ with a limited lifetime, from ~2 ss to 14 ss (Oteíza et al., 2008), seminal work unveiled that the zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle is dispensable for left-right establishment after 10 somite stages (ss) (Essner et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Essner et al., 2005.

claim: An asymmetry in dand5 gene expression is first detected at 8 ss in zebrafish.
source: Guided by this finding, most subsequent studies have been performed at 8–10 ss, when an asymmetry in dand5 gene expression is first detected (Lopes et al., 2010; Sampaio et al., 2014; Ferreira et al., 2017; Ferreira et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lopes et al., 2010; Sampaio et al., 2014; Ferreira et al., 2017; Ferreira et al., 2019.

claim: The decrease of dand5 gene expression on the left side of the LRO is the first asymmetric molecular signal in left-right development, downstream of fluid flow.
source: The decrease of dand5 gene expression on the left side of the LRO is the first asymmetric molecular signal in left-right development, downstream of fluid flow, an event conserved across species (Marques et al., 2004; Hojo et al., 2007; Schweickert et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Marques et al., 2004; Hojo et al., 2007; Schweickert et al., 2010.

claim: Intraciliary calcium oscillations (ICOs) can be registered in LRO cells as soon as zebrafish LRO cilia are formed and some start beating, at around 1–4 ss.
source: Yuan and colleagues have shown that, as soon as zebrafish LRO cilia are formed and some start beating, at around 1–4 ss, intraciliary calcium oscillations (ICOs) can be registered in LRO cells (Yuan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2015.

claim: Intraciliary calcium signals precede cytosolic calcium elevations that extend mostly to the left mesendodermal regions and are essential to trigger correct left-right patterning.
source: These signals were reported to precede cytosolic calcium elevations that extend mostly to the left mesendodermal regions and were shown to be essential to trigger correct left-right patterning.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2015 (implied from context).

claim: Fluid flow has a critical role in conveying a LR biased signal to the nearby cells.
source: Although it is evident from pioneer studies using mouse mutants without cilia or with immotile cilia that fluid flow has a critical role in conveying a LR biased signal to the nearby cells (Nonaka et al., 1998; Supp et al., 1999), both the nature of the signal and its detection mechanism remain elusive.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nonaka et al., 1998; Supp et al., 1999.

claim: The nature of the signal and its detection mechanism for left-right symmetry breaking remain elusive.
source: Although it is evident from pioneer studies using mouse mutants without cilia or with immotile cilia that fluid flow has a critical role in conveying a LR biased signal to the nearby cells (Nonaka et al., 1998; Supp et al., 1999), both the nature of the signal and its detection mechanism remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific knowledge.

claim: The mechanosensory hypothesis postulates that fluid flow can be mechanically sensed by cilia through a Polycystin protein complex involving PKD1L1 and PKD2 cation channel.
source: The mechanosensory hypothesis postulates that fluid flow can be mechanically sensed by cilia, through a Polycystin protein complex involving PKD1L1 and PKD2 cation channel (Field et al., 2011; Kamura et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Field et al., 2011; Kamura et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2015.

claim: The chemosensory hypothesis posits that vesicular parcels or extracellular vesicles containing an unknown chemical determinant are transported by the directional fluid flow towards the left side of the mouse node.
source: Conversely, the chemosensory hypothesis posits that vesicular parcels or extracellular vesicles containing an unknown chemical determinant are transported by the directional fluid flow towards the left side of the mouse node (Cartwright et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cartwright et al., 2020.

claim: The existence of a signaling morphogen in the LRO has not yet been confirmed.
source: However, the existence of such signaling morphogen has not yet been confirmed or any evidence for extra-cellular vesicle endocytosis or content release has ever been revealed with the exception of the work from Hirokawa's lab (Tanaka et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific evidence.

claim: It is virtually impossible to perform genetic manipulations of the LRO cell secretion pathway without impacting cilia length or motility.
source: The difficulty in testing which hypothesis is correct relies on the fact that it is virtually impossible to perform genetic manipulations of the LRO cell secretion pathway without impacting cilia length or motility.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental limitations based on biological knowledge.

claim: Any perturbation in lipid or protein trafficking affects motile cilia function.
source: This is not surprising if we think that any perturbation in lipid or protein trafficking affects motile cilia function, which reflects an experimental impossibility, because to test chemosensation we need to keep fluid mechanics constant.
evidence: This is a statement based on biological knowledge.

claim: The LRO is filled with fluid, but the nature of the fluid content is unknown.
source: The LRO is filled with fluid, but the nature of the fluid content is unknown because, so far, its minute volume, around one hundred picolitres (Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015), prevented a detailed biochemical analysis.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, with citation to Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015 for the volume measurement.

claim: The LRO volume is around one hundred picolitres.
source: The LRO is filled with fluid, but the nature of the fluid content is unknown because, so far, its minute volume, around one hundred picolitres (Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015), prevented a detailed biochemical analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015.

claim: The swelling mechanism of the LRO lumen is driven by the chloride channel known as cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR).
source: However, the swelling mechanism of the LRO lumen is known to be driven by the chloride channel known as cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) that, when impaired, predictably leads to empty LROs and left-right defects (Navis et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Navis et al., 2013.

claim: When CFTR is impaired, it predictably leads to empty LROs and left-right defects.
source: However, the swelling mechanism of the LRO lumen is known to be driven by the chloride channel known as cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) that, when impaired, predictably leads to empty LROs and left-right defects (Navis et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Navis et al., 2013.

claim: Total fluid extractions from the LRO were performed at different developmental time points only 30 min apart.
source: We performed total fluid extractions from the LRO at different developmental time points only 30 min apart.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The time-window for symmetry breaking was narrowed to 1-hr, from 4 to 6 ss.
source: This approach led us to narrow the time-window for symmetry breaking to 1-hr, from 4 to 6 ss, corresponding to the cell rearrangement period mechanistically explained by Wang et al., 2011 and initially noted by Kreiling et al., 2007 and Okabe et al., 2008.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The 4 to 6 ss time-window corresponds to the cell rearrangement period mechanistically explained by Wang et al., 2011 and initially noted by Kreiling et al., 2007 and Okabe et al., 2008.
source: This approach led us to narrow the time-window for symmetry breaking to 1-hr, from 4 to 6 ss, corresponding to the cell rearrangement period mechanistically explained by Wang et al., 2011 and initially noted by Kreiling et al., 2007 and Okabe et al., 2008.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2011; Kreiling et al., 2007; Okabe et al., 2008.

claim: During the 4 to 6 ss time interval, fluid flow was found to be mild but already directional.
source: During this time interval, we found fluid flow to be mild but already directional.
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Extraction of LRO fluid at 5 ss led to 35% of WT embryos with both heart and liver incorrect localization.
source: Extraction of LRO fluid at 5 ss led to 35% of WT embryos with both heart and liver incorrect localization.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Embryos did not develop LR defects when the original KV fluid was replaced with Danieau's buffer.
source: Embryos did not develop LR defects when the original KV fluid was replaced with Danieau's buffer, but LR axis was perturbed when viscosity of the same buffer was increased.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: LR axis was perturbed when viscosity of Danieau's buffer was increased.
source: Embryos did not develop LR defects when the original KV fluid was replaced with Danieau's buffer, but LR axis was perturbed when viscosity of the same buffer was increased.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Cilia number, length and anterior-posterior (A/P) distribution were not perturbed after fluid extraction at 5 ss, in fixed samples at 8 ss.
source: Controls for these experiments included confirmation that cilia number, length and anterior-posterior (A/P) distribution were not perturbed after fluid extraction at 5 ss, in fixed samples at 8 ss (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and that number of motile / immotile cilia and their A/P distribution was not changed when evaluated by live imaging at 6 ss (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a control finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Number of motile / immotile cilia and their A/P distribution was not changed after fluid extraction when evaluated by live imaging at 6 ss.
source: Controls for these experiments included confirmation that cilia number, length and anterior-posterior (A/P) distribution were not perturbed after fluid extraction at 5 ss, in fixed samples at 8 ss (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and that number of motile / immotile cilia and their A/P distribution was not changed when evaluated by live imaging at 6 ss (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a control finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: At 6 ss, no significant difference in cilia beat frequency was found between Sham controls (38.93 Hz) and fluid extracted embryos (37.85 Hz).
source: At 6 ss, no significant difference was found between Sham controls with an average of 38.93 Hz (n=56 cilia; 6 embryos) and fluid extracted embryos with 37.85 Hz (n=60 cilia; 6 embryos); (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cilia from control 'Sham' embryos at 6 ss were predominantly motile (82±4 SEM %) and localized preferentially to the anterior half of the LRO.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Tavares et al., 2017), cilia from control 'Sham' embryos at 6 ss (n=7) were predominantly motile (82±4 SEM %) and localized preferentially to the anterior half of the LRO (Fisher test, P-value <0.05, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2, consistent with citation to Tavares et al., 2017.

claim: In the manipulated group at 6 ss, motile cilia were more abundant (78 ± 10 %) and were distributed more anteriorly.
source: Similarly, in the manipulated group (n=6 embryos), motile cilia were more abundant (78 ± 10 %) and were distributed more anteriorly (Fisher test p-value <0.05; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: No significant differences were found for the ratio of motile / immotile cilia between manipulated group compared to 'Sham' controls.
source: Therefore, no significant differences were found for the ratio of motile / immotile cilia between manipulated group compared to 'Sham' controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Fluid extraction at 3 ss resulted in 2/13 embryos (15%) with both heart and liver misplacements.
source: Although most embryos recovered the fluid extraction procedure without LR defects (Figure 1B), some presented both heart and liver misplacements, starting with intervention at 3 ss (2/13 embryos, 15%, p-value = 0.235), becoming more pronounced for intervention at 4 ss (7/26 embryos, 27%, Fisher test, p-value = 0.002) and peaking with intervention at 5 ss (14/40 embryos, 35%; Fisher test, p-value = 6.44e-7).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Fluid extraction at 4 ss resulted in 7/26 embryos (27%) with both heart and liver misplacements.
source: Although most embryos recovered the fluid extraction procedure without LR defects (Figure 1B), some presented both heart and liver misplacements, starting with intervention at 3 ss (2/13 embryos, 15%, p-value = 0.235), becoming more pronounced for intervention at 4 ss (7/26 embryos, 27%, Fisher test, p-value = 0.002) and peaking with intervention at 5 ss (14/40 embryos, 35%; Fisher test, p-value = 6.44e-7).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Fluid extraction at 5 ss resulted in 14/40 embryos (35%) with both heart and liver misplacements.
source: Although most embryos recovered the fluid extraction procedure without LR defects (Figure 1B), some presented both heart and liver misplacements, starting with intervention at 3 ss (2/13 embryos, 15%, p-value = 0.235), becoming more pronounced for intervention at 4 ss (7/26 embryos, 27%, Fisher test, p-value = 0.002) and peaking with intervention at 5 ss (14/40 embryos, 35%; Fisher test, p-value = 6.44e-7).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: LR organ misplacements became progressively non-significant from 6 ss onwards (4/27 embryos, 19%).
source: LR organ misplacements then became progressively non-significant from 6 ss onwards (4/27 embryos, 19%; Fisher test, p-value = 0.865; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In wildtype embryos, zebrafish dand5 is mainly expressed on the right side of the LRO at 8 ss.
source: It is well established that in WT embryos, zebrafish dand5 is mainly expressed on the right side of the LRO at 8 ss (Lopes et al., 2010) due to left-sided decrease of dand5 mRNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lopes et al., 2010.

claim: dand5 expression became abnormally bilateral in 35% of embryos manipulated at 5 ss (6/17 manipulated embryos compared to 0/26 controls).
source: We observed that dand5 expression also became abnormally bilateral in 35% of the cases (6/17 manipulated embryos compared to 0/26 controls, Fisher test, p-value = 0.002; Figure 1C) suggesting that either lack of fluid flow or depletion of a molecular signal prevented left-sided degradation of dand5 mRNA.
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: An additional fluid extraction at 7 ss after first intervention at 5 ss showed a similar proportion of bilateral dand5 expression (6/16, 37.5%) to that observed at 5 ss.
source: Next, to further challenge the system we performed an additional fluid extraction 1 hr after the first intervention when enough liquid was replenished, at 7 ss. Results showed a similar proportion of bilateral dand5 expression (6/16, 37.5%) to that observed at 5 ss (comparing both plots in Figure 1C, Fisher test p-value = 0.728).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fluid extractions at 7 ss no longer affect LR development significantly.
source: This experiment confirmed that fluid extractions at 7 ss no longer affect LR development significantly, as already implied in Figure 1B.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The lumen of manipulated LROs started to expand soon after fluid extraction.
source: The lumen of manipulated LROs started to expand soon after fluid extraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), indicating that the fluid secretion machinery mediated by CFTR (Navis et al., 2013; Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015) was not collaterally affected by the manipulation procedure and was able to drive the swelling of the LRO lumen.
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The fluid secretion machinery mediated by CFTR was not collaterally affected by the manipulation procedure and was able to drive the swelling of the LRO lumen.
source: The lumen of manipulated LROs started to expand soon after fluid extraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), indicating that the fluid secretion machinery mediated by CFTR (Navis et al., 2013; Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015) was not collaterally affected by the manipulation procedure and was able to drive the swelling of the LRO lumen.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and citations to Navis et al., 2013; Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015.

claim: Below 1300 μm2 of KV cross-sectional area at 8 ss, LR patterning could be compromised.
source: Gokey et al., 2016 showed that below 1300 μm2 of KV cross-sectional area at 8 ss, LR patterning could be compromised.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gokey et al., 2016.

source: Further, our results showed that the LRO area was similar as well as the area change per somite (t-test, pvalue >0.05) in manipulated embryos that developed a normal organ patterning ('No Defects' group) and those that developed incorrect LR axis establishment 'Defects' group, (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, C).

claim: The general pattern of fluid flow in the LRO is roughly circular with local variations.
source: Flow can be determined by following native particles in KV as a proxy for tracking fluid directly. The general pattern of fluid flow in the LRO is roughly circular with local variations (Sampaio et al., 2014; see Figure 2—video 1 for an embryo that developed normal LR development and Figure 2—video 2 for an embryo that showed abnormal LR development).
evidence: This is a statement based on citation to Sampaio et al., 2014 and videos shown in Figure 2—video 1 and Figure 2—video 2.

claim: Linear mixed effects regression identified a significant reduction of angular velocity in the 'Defects group' (p-value = 1.2e-5, coefficient –0.13 rad/s).
source: The linear mixed regression for experiments with fluid extraction and 'Sham' intervention at 5 ss identified the following significant fixed (embryo-independent) effects: (i) a significant reduction of angular velocity in the 'Defects group' (p-value = 1.2e-5, coefficient –0.13 rad/s), (ii) greater angular velocity in the anterior compared with posterior region of the LRO (p-value = 6.3e-98, coefficient 0.16 rad/s), (iii) increased flow velocity over time (p-value = 7.1e-6, coefficient 0.021 rad/s/stage), (iv) enhanced left-right difference in the 'No Defects group' (p-value = 0.006, coefficient 0.027 rad/s), (v) reduced posterior-anterior difference in the 'Defects group' (p-value = 9.5e-5, coefficient –0.041 rad/s), (vi) enhanced posterior-anterior difference in the 'No Defects group' (p-value = 0.002, coefficient 0.034 rad/s), (vii) enhanced degree of velocity increase over time in the 'No Defects' group (p-value = 2.3e-5, coefficient 0.027 rad/s/stage) and (viii) (at marginal significance level) some degree of velocity increase over time in the 'Defects group' (p-value = 0.041, coefficient 0.013 rad/s/stage).
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on statistical analysis of experimental data.
